search_notes: Re-check 2026-10-09. CELESTIMO (GO42909). Roche media release of 17 Sep 2026 opened: the study 'met its primary endpoint at the interim analysis', with a statistically significant and clinically meaningful PFS improvement; OS immature; no numbers; names NCT04712097; data to be presented at an upcoming meeting. Looked for an earlier disclosure in Roche's documents of the two quarters before: the Q1 2026 slides with appendix (23 Apr 2026, assets.roche.com/f/176343/x/75c58a5152/irp260423.pdf) and the half-year 2026 slides with appendix (23 Jul 2026, assets.roche.com/f/176343/x/24b5ddb84d/irp260723.pdf) both list 'Ph III CELESTIMO' among the clinical results still expected in 2026, and the trial slide carries no result line in either (status 'FPI Q4 2021' in April; 'FPI Q4 2021; Recruitment completed Q2 2025' in July). The result was therefore first stated between 23 Jul and 17 Sep 2026, and the 17 Sep release is the first document found; one web search returned only coverage dated 17 to 19 Sep 2026. No earlier disclosure found, so the earlier date a model gave is not supported. No hazard ratio is public yet: Europe PMC by NCT (33 records, reviews) and Crossref titles show no result abstract. Registry (API): active not recruiting, no results, updated 2026-10-08.

Re-check 2026-10-09. SURTORI-01 (2021-012-00CH1; surufatinib plus toripalimab vs FOLFIRI, second-line NEC; acronym not in the registry). No result and no termination statement found. HUTCHMED documents read in full text from HKEX: the 2024 interim results (31 Jul 2024) list 'Surufatinib + toripalimab, SURTORI-01: 2L NEC, China, III, Ongoing since 2021, NCT05015621'; the 2024 full-year results (19 Mar 2025), the 2024 annual report (7 Apr 2025), the 2025 interim results (7 Aug 2025), the 2025 full-year results (5 Mar 2026) and the 2026 interim results (30 Jul 2026) contain no mention of SURTORI, of neuroendocrine carcinoma or of this registry number. EDGAR full-text search for 'SURTORI-01': 14 filings, the last dated 2024-07-31, none after. So the trial left the pipeline table between 31 Jul 2024 and 19 Mar 2025 with no reason given. Registry (API): status unknown, no results, not updated since 2023-12-13. Europe PMC by NCT and by acronym (reviews only), Crossref titles on surufatinib since mid-2024 (phase 2 and case reports only) and two web searches (English, Chinese) found nothing. Not checked: China's CDE trial register and Junshi's (toripalimab) documents, where a termination could be recorded, hence medium. Reads as a quiet discontinuation, but no source says the trial was stopped, so primary_result is left blank rather than terminated_no_analysis.

which_endpoint: PFS (primary per sponsor; hierarchical, TPS>=50% then TPS>=1%): reported only for the TPS>=50% subset; ALC change (second registry primary) reported as significant
search_notes: Re-check 2026-10-09. QUILT-2.023 (N-803 = nogapendekin alfa inbakicept, Anktiva). Sources conflict on what analysis this is, so the row stays unclear. (1) ImmunityBio release of 13 Jan 2026, opened on the company site (page published 2026-01-13; ir.immunitybio.com refused or timed out): 'positive results'; in first-line NSCLC a significant, sustained ALC increase with ANKTIVA plus CPI vs CPI alone (p=0.0065); 'The primary endpoint was progression-free survival ... Enrollment was closed early following changes in the first-line NSCLC treatment landscape'; no PFS result. (2) Form 10-K filed 23 Feb 2026 (read through the page-fetch tool): same ALC result, no PFS. (3) ASCO 2026 abstract 8588 (JCO suppl, published online 27 May 2026, https://ascopubs.org/doi/10.1200/JCO.2026.44.16_suppl.8588) and the company's poster PDF (image only, read by eye): 'results from 98 enrolled subjects were unblinded for exploratory analysis'; primary efficacy endpoint PFS with hierarchical testing (TPS>=50% then TPS>=1%), ALC change called a co-primary on the poster; Cohort A (N=63) ALC p=0.0065; in TPS>=50% (N=45 in the abstract, 24 vs 23 on the poster) median PFS 7.0 vs 2.2 months, HR 0.40 (95% CI 0.17-0.94), p=0.0298, 'PFS was analyzed at 8 months'; no PFS given for TPS>=1%; pooled chemotherapy cohorts B+C (N=36) PFS HR 0.48 (0.19-1.23), p=0.1192, OS HR 0.38 (0.15-0.98). The abstract calls these 'interim findings' and says 'Enrollment and follow-up are ongoing', while the registry (API, updated 2026-05-26) says Terminated, 102 enrolled, primary completion 2025-10-13, no results posted, and the January release says enrolment closed early. Not coded met: the only significant PFS figure is a subset of about 45 patients from an analysis the sponsor itself calls exploratory, and the second hierarchical step is not reported; a strict reading of the registry (ALC is listed as a primary outcome and was significant) would give met. HR cells left blank for the same reason; the subset HR is given here. The registry's version history could not be read (history endpoint returned 403), so when ALC was added as a primary outcome is not known.

which_endpoint: ORR by IRRC (one of two registry primaries; called significantly higher, no p-value); OS (other primary): medians only, no test or HR reported
search_notes: Re-check 2026-10-09. CIBI310C301 (IBI310 = ipilimumab N01, Tabosun, plus sintilimab vs sorafenib). ASCO 2026 abstract 4148 read in full (Crossref record of the DOI and the JCO page, 'Published online: May 27, 2026'; the ASCO meeting library probably released it some days earlier, not verified). 'Primary end points included overall survival (OS) and objective response rate (ORR) assessed by the IRRC'. IBI310 dose changed during the study, giving three groups: G1 3 mg/kg (n=84), G2 1 mg/kg (n=145), G3 sorafenib (n=115). 'Confirmed ORRs were significantly higher in the combination therapy groups (G1: 41.7%; G2: 22.1%) versus the control group (2.6%)'; median OS 44.0, 36.1 and 22.9 months; median PFS 13.5, 6.1 and 2.8 months; conclusion 'demonstrated survival benefits'. No hazard ratio, no p-value and no statement that OS met its boundary. Coded met on ORR because the source states a significant benefit on a registry primary endpoint; a reader who requires the OS result, or a p-value, would keep this unclear, hence medium. HR cells blank: no hazard ratio is public. Earlier disclosure looked for and not found: Innovent's 2024 annual results (26 Mar 2025), 2025 interim results (27 Aug 2025) and 2025 annual results (26 Mar 2026) do not mention the HCC trial; the 2026 interim results (25 Aug 2026) say only that the results 'were presented at the 2026 ASCO Annual Meeting (Abstract #4148)'; Innovent HKEX announcements Jan 2025 to Oct 2026 listed by title, none on this trial; one Chinese web search found only the abstract title. Registry (API): completed, primary completion 2025-12-31, no results. A new phase 3 in the same setting (NCT07490262, with bevacizumab) appears in a search summary only.

Re-check 2026-10-09. FHND9041-III-01 (FHND9041 = adonertinib, third-generation EGFR inhibitor, vs afatinib, first line; superiority, open label). First trace found nothing; the result is in a Research Square preprint, 'posted 02 Jul, 2026' on the page (opened in the browser pane; Crossref record of the DOI 10.21203/rs.3.rs-10115031/v1 created 2026-07-03), found through Europe PMC by NCT number. 175 vs 171 patients enrolled Nov 2021 to Mar 2023; data cutoff 15 Mar 2025; median PFS 16.7 vs 14.5 months, HR 0.70 (95% CI 0.54-0.91), p=0.0087; 'significantly improved PFS'; cites NCT06759857 and ChiCTR2100050397. The abstract does not say whether PFS was by central review. Source type is 'other' because it is a preprint, not peer reviewed. Earlier disclosure looked for and not found: Crossref titles on FHND9041 or adonertinib show only phase 1/2 abstracts (AACR 2023, WCLC 2025, a withdrawn ESMO 2025 abstract) and a drug-interaction paper; the sponsor's parent, Sino Biopharmaceutical, does not mention FHND9041 in its 2024 annual, 2025 interim, 2025 annual or 2026 interim results (HKEX); one Chinese web search found no filing notice or congress report. Medium because 15 months passed between data cutoff and preprint, and a Chinese congress presentation (CSCO is not indexed) or an NMPA filing notice may predate it. Registry (API): registered Jan 2025 for a trial started Aug 2021, never updated, no results.

Re-check 2026-10-09. HS-10241-301 (HS-10241 = dalmelitinib, plus aumolertinib vs platinum-pemetrexed). No statement of the phase 3 PFS result found. Hansoh HKEX documents read: voluntary announcement of 27 Feb 2026 (NDA for dalmelitinib plus aumolertinib accepted by the NMPA in exactly this population; no study named, no result); 2024 annual results (21 Mar 2025: the combination 'has also entered the phase III pivotal registration clinical trial'); 2025 interim results (18 Aug 2025: no mention); 2025 annual results (29 Mar 2026) and 2026 interim results (26 Aug 2026): the NDA acceptance and the single-arm phase 1b data shown at ELCC in Mar 2026 (n=115, median PFS 7.4 months), nothing on the randomised trial. Hansoh announcements Jan 2024 to Oct 2026 listed by title: the company issues a notice when a phase 3 meets its primary endpoint (aumolertinib Oct 2024, HS-20093 Jul 2026 twice, HS-10374 Sep 2026) and there is none for HS-10241. Europe PMC by NCT and drug names (reviews and the phase 1 paper), Crossref titles on aumolertinib, almonertinib and dalmelitinib since mid-2025 (only the ELCC phase 1b abstract 31P) and two web searches found no phase 3 readout; a search summary of OncLive's ELCC report says phase 3 results 'will be forthcoming'. The filing may well rest on this trial, which would imply a positive result, but no source says so. Not checked: WCLC 2026 and ESMO 2026 abstracts (not yet in Crossref) and China's CDE register, hence medium. Registry (API): status unknown, not updated since 2023-11-01.

Re-check 2026-10-09. HR070803-301 (Hengrui irinotecan liposome (II) plus oxaliplatin and 5-FU/LV vs nab-paclitaxel plus gemcitabine, first line, OS). No result found. Registry (API): status unknown, last known recruiting, start 2023-06-13, no results, not updated since 2024-05-09. Hengrui's news list (hengrui.com/media, 738 items, 2021-05 to 2026-10-01) has no item on first-line pancreatic cancer or on a phase 3 result for irinotecan liposome. Hengrui 2025 annual results (HKEX, 26 Mar 2026) list 'Irinotecan liposome, combination therapy, first-line treatment of advanced pancreatic cancer' among the 28 programmes that ENTERED phase III during 2025; the registry shows what that is: a sibling trial, HR070803-308 / NCT07238283, same regimen and comparator, 662 patients, started 2025-12-02, OS primary. A second phase 3 of the same design opening in late 2025 suggests this trial did not run to a usable analysis, but no source says it was stopped or what it showed, so primary_result is left blank. The 2026 interim results (19 Aug 2026) mention the liposome only as a marketed product. Europe PMC by NCT (0 records), Crossref titles on HR070803 (second-line PAN-HEROIC-1, a phase 1 in first-line pancreatic cancer, colorectal phase 2 abstracts) and one Chinese web search found no readout. Do not attach PAN-HEROIC-1 (second line, met OS) to this row. Not checked: Hengrui's Shanghai exchange notices and China's CDE register, hence medium.

Re-check 2026-10-09. SHR-A1811-310 (SHR-A1811 = trastuzumab rezetecan, first-line HER2-mutant NSCLC, PFS by BICR). Not read out. Registry (API): recruiting, estimated primary completion 2026-02, updated 2026-01-21, no results. Hengrui 2026 interim results (HKEX, 19 Aug 2026): the pipeline table as of 31 Jul 2026 still lists 'First-line treatment of HER2-mutated advanced or metastatic non-small cell lung cancer' as a development indication, and it is not among the NDA acceptances of the period; the only lung indication approved is second line. Hengrui's news list (hengrui.com/media) read to 2026-10-01: 'met primary endpoint' items exist for other trials of this drug (HER2-positive breast cancer, 1 Sep 2026) and for other products, none for HER2-mutant NSCLC. Europe PMC by NCT (10 records, reviews) and by study number (0), Crossref titles on SHR-A1811 and rezetecan since mid-2025 (a randomised phase 2 first-line cohort at AACR 2026, CT301, which is a sibling study from the phase 1b/2 trial and not this one) and one Chinese web search found no phase 3 result; the search summary notes a breakthrough-therapy listing for the first-line indication in Feb 2026 (not opened).

which_endpoint: PuFS (registry primary): no statistically significant difference; OS (dual primary per the abstract): HR given, not stated as significant
search_notes: Re-check 2026-10-09. COREMAP (SIM-372-ENDO-301; Endostar plus intracavitary cisplatin vs placebo plus cisplatin). ESMO GI 2026 abstract 673P read in full on the Annals of Oncology page (opened in the browser pane; the page-fetch tool got 403): 'Final analysis', cutoff 10 Feb 2025, 434 randomised, 428 treated (216 vs 212). 'Dual primary endpoints were OS and puncture and/or drainage free survival (PuFS)'. Result: 'clinically meaningful improvements in OS (median 7.8 vs 5.6; HR, 0.807; 95% CI, 0.625, 1.042; Peto P=0.0338)' and 'no statistically significant difference in PuFS'. Coded not_met: the registry's only primary endpoint (PuFS) is stated as not significant, and OS is described as clinically meaningful, never as statistically significant, with a 95% CI that includes 1. The abstract gives no significance boundary for OS, so a reader could argue OS was met at a split alpha; hence medium. HR CELLS ARE FOR OS, not PuFS (no PuFS hazard ratio is given). Date: the page's citation date is 2026/07/01 (Ann Oncol vol 37 suppl 1, July 2026) and ESMO's site gives the congress as 1 to 4 July 2026; the poster day was not verified and the DOI was registered at Crossref on 16 July, the date the first trace used. Earlier disclosure looked for and not found in Simcere's HKEX documents: 2024 annual results (24 Mar 2025: last patient in Nov 2024), 2025 interim results (21 Aug 2025: pipeline row only), 2025 annual results (25 Mar 2026: NDA for thoracoabdominal effusions accepted Feb 2026, no result; 2025 data releases list other Endostar studies only), 2026 interim results (20 Aug 2026: study presented at ESMO GI in July 2026, no result stated); Simcere announcements Jan 2025 to Oct 2026 listed by title, none on this trial. Three web searches found no other report. Registry (API): active not recruiting, primary completion 2025-02-10, no results.

Re-check 2026-10-09. JP001-GM-001 (JP001 = Siroquine; Johnpro Biotech, Taiwan; licensee HebaBiz). Nothing found that states or hints at a result of the OS analysis; the first trace's 'unclear' is changed to no. Registry (API): status unknown, estimated enrolment 288, no results, not updated since 2021-05-11. Johnpro's website (johnpro.com.tw, opened) is static: the JP001 page says only that the drug entered a phase 2/3 trial in 2017, and the investor page's latest entry is dated 2020/10/19. A HebaBiz release of Aug 2021 (reposted copy opened, 1stoncology.com/blog/?p=62751) reports FDA clearance, 370 patients planned across Taiwan, the US and mainland China, and 'Six patients so far have been randomly recruited into the study arm'; its remark that PFS and OS were 'observed to be significantly higher' rests on that handful of patients and is not a trial result. Europe PMC by NCT (7 reviews), by JP001 and by Siroquine, Crossref titles (none) and two web searches (traditional Chinese, English) found nothing later than 2021. HebaBiz's site did not respond. Medium: Taiwanese company filings and news were reached only through one web search. The trial may never have enrolled beyond a few patients; no source says it was stopped.

Re-check 2026-10-09. KRT-232-118 (ENGOT-en21 / GOG-3089; navtemadlin maintenance, phase 2/3). Terminated by the sponsor a year after it started, before the phase 3 part. The EU register (CTIS record 2022-502196-31-00, read through euclinicaltrials.eu/ctis-public-api/retrieve/2022-502196-31-00) gives status Ended, an EARLY_TERMINATION event dated 2024-07-26 in each of 15 member states with reason 'Sponsor Decision', and global end of trial 2024-08-29; a summary of results was submitted on 2025-10-07 but its document could not be opened. The trial began in July 2023 with a 12-month dose-selection Part 1, so the Part 2 comparison of PFS against placebo (the phase 3 primary endpoint) cannot have been analysed. ClinicalTrials.gov (API) still says recruiting and has not been updated since 2024-05-02. Kartos, now 'an Ipsen company', lists only myelofibrosis studies on its research page and no endometrial presentation on its publications page (both opened). Europe PMC by NCT and study numbers (reviews), Crossref titles on navtemadlin (no endometrial result), EDGAR full-text search for the study number (0; navtemadlin plus endometrial appears only in a competitor's annual reports) and one web search found no result and no announcement of the termination. Phase 2/3 with a dose-finding first part: review for exclusion.

Re-check 2026-10-09. ASPIRE (CL-SBP-101-04; SBP-101 = ivospemin). Ended early with no result disclosed. The EU register (CTIS record 2024-514714-12-00, which cites NCT05254171; read through euclinicaltrials.eu/ctis-public-api/retrieve/2024-514714-12-00) gives status Ended and an EARLY_TERMINATION event dated 2025-03-28 in all six member states (Austria, Belgium, France, Germany, Italy, Spain) with reason 'Sponsor Decision', and no results. The sponsor stopped reporting at the same time: EDGAR lists an 8-K of 22 Jan 2025 (Items 2.04 and 5.01, not opened), an 8-K of 18 Feb 2025 cutting the two officers' salaries (opened), no company filing after that (a Schedule 13D/A of 24 Apr 2025 could not be opened), and an SEC order of 29 Sep 2025 declaring a registration statement abandoned because the company did not respond (opened); the company website does not answer. EDGAR full-text search for ivospemin or SBP-101 in 2025-2026 returns no Panbela filing. An interim analysis had been expected in the first quarter of 2025 (search summary of the company's 2024 statements, not opened); nothing found says whether it was run, so the termination is recorded as terminated_no_analysis on the register's stated reason, and the row is medium because an undisclosed interim result cannot be ruled out. Europe PMC by NCT (reviews and retinal-toxicity case reports), Crossref titles on ivospemin and one web search found no result. ClinicalTrials.gov (API) still says recruiting, not updated since 2024-11-06.

Re-check 2026-10-09. ICT-107-301. No primary analysis exists to disclose. ImmunoCellular Therapeutics announced on 21 Jun 2017 (8-K exhibit, read through the page-fetch tool) that it would suspend further randomisation because it could not secure the money to complete the trial; the latest ICT-107 filing among those EDGAR full-text search returned is dated Aug 2018. The registry (API), now under Precision Life Sciences Group, says Suspended, 'Company is discussing with FDA to reinitiate the trial now', with enrolment still an estimate (234), a start date re-entered as 2024-12 and primary completion 2025-12, no results, not updated since 2024-04-03. Europe PMC by NCT (51 records, reviews) and one web search found no result and no restart. Not coded terminated_no_analysis because the registry says suspended, not terminated, and no source says the trial was abandoned; in substance it stopped in 2017 for lack of funds.

Re-check 2026-10-09. QL1203-003 (QL1203 is a panitumumab biosimilar; add-on to mFOLFOX6 vs placebo, superiority). First trace found nothing; the result is ASCO GI 2025 abstract 190 (J Clin Oncol 43, 4_suppl), found by a Crossref title query on QL1203 and read in full in the Crossref, OpenAlex and Semantic Scholar records and on the JCO page (browser pane): planned interim analysis at 338 of 416 PFS events, cutoff 22 Mar 2024, 641 randomised (426 vs 215); median PFS by blinded independent review 11.20 vs 8.34 months, HR 0.61 (97.42% CI 0.47-0.79), one-sided p<0.0001; 'significantly improved PFS'; cites NCT04233151. The interval in the HR cells is the 97.42% CI of the interim analysis, not a 95% CI. Date is the JCO page's 'Published online: January 27, 2025'; the symposium abstracts were probably released a few days earlier (a search summary dates the result 23 Jan 2025), not verified. Lag is against an estimated registry date of 2024-12-31, while the data cutoff was Mar 2024. A filing in China in Aug 2024 and a later approval appear in a web-search summary only (not opened); a filing notice would not state the result, and Qilu is privately held with no exchange notices. Registry (API): status unknown, not updated since 2023-05-26, no results. Biosimilar tested for superiority over placebo: review for exclusion if biosimilar trials are out of scope.
